{{Short description|German mathematician and teacher}}

'''Hans Heinrich Bürmann''' (died 21 June 1817, in [[Mannheim]]) was a German [[mathematician]] and teacher. He ran an "academy of commerce" in Mannheim since 1795 where he taught mathematics.<ref name="adb"/> He also served as a censor in Mannheim.<ref name="adb"/> He was nominated Headmaster of the Commerce Academy of the [[Grand Duchy of Baden]] in 1811. He did scientific research in the area of [[combinatorics]] and he contributed to the development of the symbolic language of mathematics. He discovered the generalized form of the [[Lagrange inversion theorem]]. He corresponded and published with [[Joseph Louis Lagrange]] and [[Carl Hindenburg]].

==Iterate function composition notation==
The [[function composition|compositional]] notation <math>f^{  n}</math> for the {{nowrap|<math>n</math>-th}} [[iterated function|iterate]] <math>f^{n} := f\circ f^{n-1} = \overbrace {f\circ f\circ\dotsb\circ f}^{n \text{ times}}</math> of function <math>f</math> was originally introduced by Bürmann{{citation needed|date=August 2020|reason=The fact is undisputable, but for historical completeness, let's find Bürmann's original work on this and add here as a citation. It must be dated significantly before 1813 (according to Herschel in 1820 und Cajori in 1929).}}<ref name="Herschel_1820"/><ref name="Cajori_1929"/> and later independently suggested by [[John Frederick William Herschel]] in 1813.<ref name="Herschel_1813"/><ref name="Herschel_1820"/><ref name="Cajori_1929"/>
